newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU commissioner fights on after fainting fit.
newsitem.headline: EU commissioner fights on after fainting fit.

text.p: When European Commissioner Emma Bonino fainted on Friday after a marathon, 21-hour meeting of EU fisheries ministers it came as little surprise to her staff.

After a year banging her head against a brick wall to get the world to help millions of refugees in Africa and EU governments to take unpopular measures to protect fishing stocks, the crunch was bound to come sometime.

Few eyebrows were raised either when, within hours, she was back in her office for a pre-Christmas party with her staff and vowing to fight on to raise the world community's consciousness on humanitarian aid needs.
"I had some sleep and now I'm back to work," she told Reuters by telephone. "I will not give up. I will keep trying to keep the consciousness of the world awake on this issue."

Bonino, a 48-year-old Italian who juggles the fisheries, humanitarian aid and consumer policy portfolios at the EU executive, has been the most vocal critic of the delay in helping refugees in Africa's Great Lakes region.
Witnessing the situation on the ground and then the world's indifference and delay in sending troops to eastern Zaire to help, had taken an emotional and physical toll, she admitted.

"It has been emotionally difficult because in the field I can see the faces of the people. As a dossier I know it completely...when we talk about Goma I see the camps, I see the faces of the children," she said.
"It's emotional, but it's also a major political frustration."

As other members of the Commission flew home for Christmas she said she planned on Sunday to send an open letter to the incoming Secretary General of the United Nations Kofi Annan, having failed to get action from his predecessor.
One of her major concerns is that international conventions guaranteeing the sanctity of United Nations refugee camps have simply not been respected.
"No one can feel safe in the future if they are in the refugee camps of the United Nations," she said.

Bonino, who was once air-lifted onto a Spanish fishing boat on the high seas during a fishing row between the EU and Canada, has been visibly irritated by questions about the price of salmon in the EU at a time when people are dying in Zaire.
She told Reuters earlier this year she did not have a conventional idea of a holiday and that politics was her passion rather than her job.
Although she enjoys scuba diving and sailing, she likes to spend five days a week in her Brussels office, and weekends and holidays in the field.
She spent last Christmas on a mission to Bethlehem, Easter under fire in Somalia and the summer dropping in on the Dalai Lama and Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi.
"The Commissioner was exhausted after two years of strenuous work without holidays. It finally caught up with her," her spokesman said of the marathon annual talks setting next year's fish catches.
She "fought to the end, gave a final speech and fainted."
